Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:10:1.hebrew: יכול יהדרנו בממון - יכול יהא הידור זה הידור ממון, לכבדו בממון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:10:1.english: One might [think] he should honor him with money - One might [think] this honor is a monetary honor, to honor him with money.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:11:1.hebrew: יכול יעצים עיניו כמי שלא ראהו - לקמן (קידושין דף לג.) פריך: אטו ברשיעי עסקינן?:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:11:1.english: One might [think] he may close his eyes like one who did not see him - Below (Kiddushin 33a), [the Gemara] asks: Are we dealing with wicked people?

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:11:2.hebrew: דבר המסור ללב - ללבו של עושה הדבר, הוא יודע אם ראהו או לאו. לפי שיכול להשמט מעיני הבריות, שלא יחזיקוהו כרשע ושידינוהו לכף זכות ויאמרו "לא ראהו", לכך נאמר: "ויראת מאלהיך" — שכל המחשבות גלויות לו, ויודע בך שלסתור ולבטל מצותו נתכוונת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:11:2.english: A matter given over to the heart - [Entrusted] to the heart of the one who does the deed: he knows whether he saw him or not. Since he can evade the eyes of people so that they will not consider him wicked and so that they will judge him favorably and say, 'He did not see him,' therefore it is stated: 'And you shall fear your God' — for all thoughts are revealed to Him, and He knows concerning you that you intended to undermine and nullify His commandment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:12:1.hebrew: שלא יטריח - אם יכול לילך דרך אחרת, שלא יעמיד את הציבור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:12:1.english: That he should not trouble [others] - If he can go by another route, so that he does not cause the public to stand.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:12:2.hebrew: זקן ויראת - להכי סמך ויראת לזקן, לומר שאף הזקן יירא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:12:2.english: An elder, and you shall fear - For this reason [the verse] juxtaposed “and you shall fear” to “an elder,” to say that the elder, too, must fear [God].

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:12:3.hebrew: כל שיבה במשמע - ואפי' זקן אשמאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:12:3.english: Any hoary head is included - Even an ignorant elder.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:13:1.hebrew: ת"ק סבר יניק וחכים לא - והכי קאמר תנא קמא: אין זקן אלא זקן שהוא חכם, שנאמר: ״אספה לי שבעים איש מזקני ישראל וגו'״. והתם זקנים וחכמים היו, כדכתיב: ״אשר ידעת כי הם וגו'״ — אלמא זקנים וידועים הוו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:13:1.english: The first tanna maintains: [One who is] young and wise [is] not [included] - And this is what the first tanna is saying: "An elder" means nothing other than an elder who is wise, as it is stated: "Gather unto Me seventy men of the elders of Israel..." (Numbers 11:16). And there, they were [both] elders and wise, as it is written: "whom you know to be [the elders of the people...]" — evidently, they were elders and distinguished [scholars].

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:13:2.hebrew: ור' יוסי הגלילי - דמשני ליה לקרא ממשמעו, זקנה ממש, ודריש ליה "זה שקנה חכמה" — סבר: אפי' יניק וחכים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:13:2.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili - Since he alters [the meaning of] the verse from its literal sense, [which is] actual old age, and expounds it [as], "This is one who has acquired wisdom" — he maintains [that it applies] even [to one who is] young and wise.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:14:1.hebrew: אי סלקא דעתך כדאמר ת"ק - דחד הוא דאיירי ביה קרא, שיבה והוא חכם — נכתוב: "מפני שיבה זקן תקום והדרת", ונגמר ג"ש. מאי שנא דפלגינהו? ש"מ תרתי מילי נינהו, וה"ק: מפני שיבה תקום והדרת, תקום והדרת פני זקן שקנה חכמה, ואפילו יניק. ומדקפיד אחכמה, אמרינן נמי: שיבה לאו זקן אשמאי קאמר, דליכא למימר רבי יוסי אזקן אשמאי נמי פליג; אם כן, היינו איסי בן יהודה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:14:1.english: If it enters your mind [to explain] as the first tanna says - that the verse is speaking of only one [person] — [namely, one of] hoary head who is [also] a sage — let it write: “Before the hoary head of an elder you shall stand and you shall revere,” and we would derive [it by] a verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah]. Why did [the verse] separate them? Learn from this [that] they are two [distinct] matters, and this is what it is saying: “Before a hoary head you shall stand and revere; [and] you shall stand and revere the face of an elder” who has acquired wisdom, and even [if he is] young. And since [the verse] is particular about wisdom, we also say [that] “hoary head” does not mean a boorish elder, for one cannot say that Rabbi Yosei also disagrees regarding a boorish elder — if so, that is [the view of] Isi ben Yehuda.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:15:1.hebrew: משום דבעי למיסמך - לומר שלא יטריח, כדלעיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:15:1.english: Because it needs to juxtapose - To say that [an elder] should not trouble [others], as [stated] above.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:15:2.hebrew: כדקאמר רבי יוסי - דתרי נינהו, נכתוב בתרוייהו קימה והידור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:15:2.english: As Rabbi Yosei says - That they are two [distinct individuals], let [the Torah] write standing and honoring for both of them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:1:1.hebrew: הכא תורה דיליה היא - בתמיה: הכבוד תלוי בתורה, ואינו יכול למחול על כבוד התורה, שהיא של הקב"ה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:1:1.english: Here, is it his Torah? - [This is asked] in wonderment: The honor is dependent on the Torah, and he cannot forgo the honor of the Torah, which belongs to the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:1:2.hebrew: ובתורתו יהגה - "כי אם בתורת ה' חפצו ובתורתו יהגה" — בתחילה היא נקראת תורת השם, ומשלמדה וגרסה, היא נקראת תורתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:1:2.english: And in his Torah he meditates - [The verse states:] “Rather, his delight is in the Torah of the Lord, and in his Torah he meditates” — at first it is called the Torah of the Lord, but once he has learned it and reviewed it, it is called his Torah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:2:1.hebrew: רבנן - אתם חכמים וחשובים בעיניכם שלא עמדתם מפני, ורבנן חביריכם דקמו מפני לאו רבנן נינהו? ובלשון תימה אמר להם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:2:1.english: Sages - [Are] you wise and important in your own eyes, that you did not stand before me, and [are] the Sages, your colleagues who stood before me, not Sages? And he said [this] to them as a rhetorical question:

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:3:1.hebrew: הידור - לנוע מעט, כאילו רוצה לעמוד מפניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:3:1.english: Reverence - To move slightly, as if one wishes to stand before him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:5:1.hebrew: לא נדמו לו אלא לערביים - שאמר להם: "ורחצו רגליכם", שהערביים משתחוים לאבק רגליהם, כדאמרן בבבא מציעא (ד' פו:): אמרו לו: "בערביים חשדתנו שמשתחוים לאבק רגליהם":
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:5:1.english: They appeared to him only as Arabs - For he said to them: “And wash your feet” (Genesis 18:4), because Arabs bow down to the dust of their feet, as we said in Bava Metzia (86b): They said to him, “Did you suspect us of being Arabs who bow down to the dust of their feet?”

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:5:2.hebrew: רבן גמליאל ברבי - כלומר, אדם גדול. וכן כל ברבי שבגמ':
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:5:2.english: Rabban Gamliel beribbi - That is to say, a great man. And likewise every [instance of] beribbi in the Gemara.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:1.hebrew: אי סלקא דעתך כדאמר ת"ק - דחד הוא דאיירי ביה קרא, שיבה והוא חכם — נכתוב: "מפני שיבה זקן תקום והדרת", ונגמר ג"ש. מאי שנא דפלגינהו? ש"מ תרתי מילי נינהו. וה"ק: מפני שיבה תקום והדרת, תקום והדרת פני זקן שקנה חכמה, ואפילו יניק. ומדקפיד אחכמה, אמרינן נמי: שיבה לאו זקן אשמאי קאמר; דליכא למימר רבי יוסי אזקן אשמאי נמי פליג, אם כן — היינו איסי בן יהודה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:1.english: If it should enter your mind [to say] as the first tanna said - That it is [only] one [person] that the verse is speaking of — [namely, one possessing] hoary age and who is wise — let [the verse] write: “Before a hoary elder you shall stand and you shall revere,” and let us derive [that he must be wise through] a gezeirah shavah. Why did [the verse] separate them? Learn from this that they are two [distinct] matters. And this is what [the verse] is saying: “Before the hoary head you shall stand and you shall revere”; [and likewise,] you shall stand and you shall revere the face of an elder who has acquired wisdom, even [if he is] young. And since [the verse] is particular about wisdom, we also say: “hoary head” does not mean an ignorant [ashmai] elder; for one cannot say that Rabbi Yosei disagrees concerning an ignorant elder as well, [for] if so, that would be [the position of] Isi ben Yehuda.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:2.hebrew: זקן אשמאי - אשם, רשע ועם הארץ:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:2.english: An ashmai elder - [One who is] guilty, wicked, and an ignoramus.

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:3.hebrew: מזקני ישראל - גמר זקן מזקני — מה להלן גדולים וחכמים, דכתיב (במדבר י״א:ט״ז) ״אשר ידעת כי הם זקני העם ושוטריו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:3.english: Of the elders of Israel - [The Tanna] derives [the meaning of] “elder” from “elders”: Just as there, [they were] prominent and wise [men], as it is written (Numbers 11:16): “Whom you know to be the elders of the people and its officers” — [so too here, an elder must be a wise man].

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:4.hebrew: אין זקן אלא זה שקנה חכמה - ולשון נוטריקון דבר הכתוב, ולקמיה פריך: היינו ת"ק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:8:4.english: “An elder” means nothing other than this [one] who has acquired wisdom - And the verse spoke in the language of a contraction [notarikon], and later on [the Gemara] asks: Isn’t this [the same as] the first Tanna?

Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:9:1.hebrew: אלא במקום שיש לו הידור - בעמידתו, דהיינו תוך ד' אמות, דמוכחא מילתא שמפניו הוא עומד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 32b:9:1.english: Only in a place where there is reverence for him - In his standing; that is, within four cubits, where the matter is evident that he is standing before him.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 32b:14:1.hebrew: מאי שנא דפלגינהו ש"מ דהאי לאו האי - וה"ק: מפני שיבה תקום והדרת, תקום והדרת פני זקן שקנה חכמה; ש"מ אפי' יניק וחכים. ופירש בקונט': מדקפיד קרא אחכמה, ש"מ דזקן לאו אשמאי, אלא בעינן חכמה בהדיה; דליכא למימר ר' יוסי נמי אזקן אשמאי פליג וקאמר דלא בעינן חכמה, דא"כ היינו איסי בן יהודה — כן פירש הקונטרס. ועוד מוסיף ר"י, דליכא למימר נמי דודאי פליג ואמר זקן אשמאי מהני, ואיסי פליג עליה ואומר אפי' סבי דארמאי, דהא "כל שיבה במשמע" קאמר — הא לא אשכחן בשום דוכתא דזקן עובד כוכבים צריך לכבדו! ועוד, דלקמן (קידושין דף לג.) קאמר דרבי יוחנן הוה קאי מקמי סבי ארמאי, ותלי טעמא ב"כמה הרפתקי עדו עלייהו", ולא קאמר משום דאיסי. וא"ת: כיון דבהדי שיבה נמי בעי חכמה כדפירש בקונטרס לרבי יוסי הגלילי דמרבה אפי' יניק וחכים, "שיבה" דכתב רחמנא למה לי? פשיטא! כיון דאפי' יניק וחכים, כ"ש שיבה וחכים; דמי גרע אם הוא זקן בהדי חכם?! וי"ל, דאי לא כתב רחמנא "שיבה", ה"א דניבעי זקן וחכם ממש, אבל יניק וחכים לא; להכי אתא "שיבה" לגלויי דלא בעינן זקן וחכים, אלא בחד לחוד סגי, אפילו יניק וחכים. ומיהו קשה, דאם כן מאי קאמר: "אי ס"ד כדקאמר ת"ק, לכתוב רחמנא מפני שיבה זקן תקום"? אדרבה, לא לכתוב אלא "זקן"! דהא נמי אמר "זקן" בלא "שיבה", "זקן" במשמעו — זקן ממש משמע! אלא ודאי "זקן" — יניק וחכים משמע, והדרא קושיא לדוכתיה. ונראה לר"י, דודאי יניק וחכים צריך שיהא מופלג, ולכך איצטריך "שיבה" אע"פ שאינו מופלג; דכך לי זקן שאינו מופלג כמו יניק וחכים שהוא מופלג. אבל אם היו שוים בחכמה, היניק והזקן — צריך שיעמוד היניק מפני הזקן; דגבי יניק צריך שיהיה מופלג בחכמה, וגבי זקן אינו צריך:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 32b:14:1.english: What is the difference that [the Merciful One] separated them? Conclude from it that this is not that - And this is what [the verse] means: "Before the hoary head you shall stand and revere; you shall stand and revere the face of an elder" who has acquired wisdom; conclude from this [that the obligation applies to] even [one who is] young and wise. And the Kuntres explained: Since the verse insists on wisdom, conclude from this that an elder is not an ignorant elder [ashmai], but rather we require wisdom alongside it [i.e., with old age]. For one cannot say that Rabbi Yosei also disagrees [with the first tanna] regarding an ignorant elder and says that we do not require wisdom, because if so, that would be [the same as the opinion of] Issi ben Yehuda. So explained the Kuntres. And the Ri adds further that one cannot also say that [Rabbi Yosei] certainly disagrees [with the first tanna] and says that an ignorant [Jewish] elder qualifies [for honor], and that Issi disagrees with him and says [that it applies] even to elderly Arameans [gentiles] — for [Issi] says: "Any hoary head is implied" — [one cannot say this, because] we do not find in any place that one is required to honor an elderly idolater! And furthermore, later (Kiddushin 33a) [the Gemara] says that Rabbi Yochanan would stand before elderly Arameans, and he attributed the reason to: "How many tribulations have passed over these [people]!" and [the Gemara] did not say [that he did so] because of Issi. And if you say: Since alongside a hoary head [Rabbi Yosei] also requires wisdom, as the Kuntres explained, according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who includes even [one who is] young and wise, why do I need "hoary head" which the Merciful One wrote? It is obvious! Since even [one who is] young and wise [must be honored], all the more so one who has a hoary head and is wise! For is he any worse if he is old in addition to being wise?! And one can say: That if the Merciful One had not written "hoary head," I would have said that we require one who is literally old and wise, but one who is young and wise, no [he would not be honored]. Therefore, "hoary head" came to reveal that we do not require [both] old and wise [in one person], but rather either one alone is sufficient, even young and wise. However, this is difficult: For if so, what is [the meaning of what the Gemara] says: "If it enters your mind [to explain] as the first tanna says, let the Merciful One write: Before the hoary head of an elder you shall stand"? On the contrary, let it write only "an elder"! For this too: if [the Torah] said "elder" without "hoary head," "elder" in its plain meaning would mean literally old! Rather, "elder" certainly means young and wise, and the difficulty returns to its place. And it appears to the Ri: That certainly, one who is young and wise must be outstanding [in wisdom], and therefore "hoary head" was needed [to teach that an elderly scholar must be honored] even though he is not outstanding; for an old man who is not outstanding is the same to me as one who is young and wise who is outstanding. But if they were equal in wisdom, the young man and the old man, the young man must stand before the old man, because regarding a young man, he must be outstanding in wisdom, whereas regarding an old man, he does not need [to be outstanding].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 32b:8:1.hebrew: זקן אשמאי - פי' בקונטרס: אשמאי — רשע ועם הארץ. וקשה, דהיכי קאמר איסי בן יהודה דשיבה משמע אפילו זקן אשמאי? והלא מצוה אפילו להכותו, לבזותו, לזלזלו! לכך פר"ת: אשמאי — לשון שוממין, כמו "פתחי שמאי" דמנחות (דף לג:), כלומר: בור ועם הארץ, כדמתרגמינן "והאדמה לא תשם" — "וארעא לא תבור" (בראשית מ״ז:י״ט):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 32b:8:1.english: "An ashmai elder" - Rashi explained in the commentary: Ashmai [means] a wicked person and an am ha'aretz [an ignorant person]. And this is difficult: For how could Isi ben Yehuda say that "hoary head" implies even an ashmai elder? Behold, it is even a mitzvah to strike him, to humiliate him, [and] to degrade him! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained: Ashmai is an expression of desolation [shomemin], like "the desolate entrances [pitkhei shammai]" in Menachot (33b) — that is to say, an uncultivated person [bur] and an am ha'aretz, as we translate: "and the land not be desolate" [as] "and the land not lie fallow" (Genesis 47:19).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 32b:8:2.hebrew: ואין זקן אלא חכם שנאמר אספה לי שבעים איש כו' - לאו גזירה שוה גמורה היא, דאם כן — ליבעו מומחין כי התם; אלא לא הוי אלא הוכחה בעלמא, דזקן אשמאי אינו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 32b:8:2.english: “And an ‘elder’ means nothing other than a wise man, as it is stated: ‘Gather unto Me seventy men,’ etc.” - This is not a formal verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah], for if so, it should require ordained experts, like there; rather, it is merely a general proof that a simple elder [zaken ashmai] is not [included].
